# Rush Hour — project memory (static: do not edit during a run; volatile state lives in STATE.md)

Five-phase chained pipeline predicting hourly bike demand `cnt`: GD → Polynomial → Bias-Variance → Regularization (L1, L2, ElasticNet) → Logistic. Authority: `Project_1_description.md`. Digest + traceability: `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/TRACE.csv`.

## Commands
- `make verify-fast` lint + tests + leak scan + chain check + trace counts (compact output)
- `make verify` adds notebook run, submission check, report number trace, strict trace
- `make all` rebuild artifacts (phase N rebuilds if anything upstream changed)
- `make fingerprint` stable artifact hashes (prove refactors preserve behavior)

## Hard constraints (a change that breaks one is rejected no matter how much it improves a metric)
H1 seed = sha256 of sorted team IDs joined by "_" mod 100000; one seeded 80/20 split; Phase 3 adds one chronological split.
H2 Fit every scaler/encoder/expansion/selector/threshold on train rows only. test.csv is only ever `transform`ed, at the end.
H3 No external data. H4 Phases 1–2: own gradient descent, no sklearn fit/predict. H5 Each phase consumes the previous phase's artifact (hash-chained).
H6 L1, L2 and Elastic Net all implemented and compared. H7 Phase 5 uses only Phase 4 survivors; label from `cnt`, group thresholds from train.
H8 Submission comes from the regression model the pipeline recommends. H9 Expectation cell committed before each phase runs; Outcome after; justification for every open choice.
H10 Notebook runs top-to-bottom; report ≤ 6 pages; every number in it traces to an artifact. H11 No tuning on test.csv; never split/shuffle it.
H12 Every team member can explain and re-run any cell: readable code, config cell at top. H13 Diagnostic models outside the course algorithms live in `exp/` only, never in the chain or the submission.

## Layout and ownership (one writer per path)
`src/` code (coder) · `tests/` (qa-engineer) · `nb/pN_*.py` percent-format cells: code cells (coder), markdown cells (chief/scribe) · `tools/` deterministic checkers (coder) · `docs/` spec, ADRs, trace (chief; verifier edits TRACE status only) · `reports/verify|analysis/` (verifier|analyst) · `exp/` experiments (experimenter, analyst) · `report/` (scribe) · `handoff/` specs, receipts, ledgers (chief + each agent its own file) · `artifacts/` written by phase code, pointer by chief.

## Working rules
- Communicate through files (`handoff/`), not pasted text. Specs name files and tests; receipts are JSON.
- Handoff/status text may be telegraphic; notebook prose, report, docstrings are plain full sentences in the team's voice.
- Never paste datasets or long output; tail logs; one-line summaries; compute once and cache to disk.
- Two failed attempts → escalate. No unrequested files, tests, refactors or review rounds.
- Do not edit this file, the agent definitions or the skills during a run (keeps the cached prefix and preserved thinking valid).
